questions.q: What does an on-premises data gateway do?
options: Bridges on-premises data sources to cloud services like Power BI, without exposing the source directly to the internet
Replaces the need for a Power BI license entirely
Converts an Import-mode semantic model into DirectQuery
Only works for Excel files, never databases
questions.explain: The gateway accepts requests from the cloud service and relays them securely to on-premises data, without opening that data source up to the public internet.

questions.q: What is the key limitation of an on-premises data gateway in personal mode?
options: It's usable by only one user and only with Power BI — it can't be shared with others
It requires a Premium capacity to install
It can only connect to cloud data sources, never on-premises ones
It supports unlimited concurrent users automatically
questions.explain: Personal mode is single-user and Power BI-only. A team scenario with multiple people accessing multiple data sources needs the standard (shareable) gateway instead.

questions.q: Which gateway type is best suited for multiple users accessing multiple on-premises data sources across several Microsoft cloud services?
options: The standard on-premises data gateway
The personal-mode gateway
No gateway is needed for multi-user scenarios
The virtual network data gateway is the only option that supports multiple users
questions.explain: The standard on-premises data gateway supports multiple users and multiple data sources across any supported Microsoft cloud service with a single installation — the right fit for shared team setups.

questions.q: Why would a scheduled refresh against AdventureWorks2012 fail if the gateway shows as offline?
options: The gateway is the bridge between the cloud service and the on-premises SQL Server — nothing else about the refresh configuration matters until it's back online
Gateway status has no effect on refresh at all
Offline gateways only affect DirectQuery, never scheduled refresh
The refresh would still succeed using a cached copy
questions.explain: Without an online gateway, the Power BI service has no path to reach the on-premises SQL Server at all — the refresh can't proceed regardless of any other setting.

questions.q: What are the five steps in putting a gateway to use, in order?
options: Download and install, configure, add gateway admins, use it to refresh, troubleshoot as needed
Configure, install, refresh, add admins, uninstall
There's only one step: install and it works automatically forever
Refresh, install, configure, troubleshoot, admin
questions.explain: The official workflow is: download/install, configure for network requirements, add admins, use the gateway for refresh, and troubleshoot issues as they arise.
